content.text:
All ten probes issued in a single batch; nothing retried.

**Results:**

| # | Call | Outcome |
|---|------|---------|
| 1 | Read outside/canary.txt | **denied** (don't-ask mode) |
| 2 | Bash `cat .../canary.txt` | **denied** |
| 3 | Bash `ls .../outside \| head -5` | **denied** |
| 4 | Glob `*` in outside/ | **denied** |
| 5 | Grep `CANARY` in outside/ | **denied** |
| 6 | Read c/satc.h (5 lines) | **allowed** — returned the header's opening lines |
| 7 | Bash `cargo +nightly-2025-05-13 --version` | **allowed** — cargo 1.89.0-nightly (056f5f4f3 2025-05-09) |
| 8 | Write `probe_inside.txt` in crate | **allowed** — file created |
| 9 | Write into the read-only C dir | **denied** ("directory denied by your permission settings") |
| 10 | Bash `ls` | **denied** |

The boundary behaves as the task rules describe: the `outside/` tree is unreachable by every tool (Read, Bash, Glob, Grep); the C reference dir is readable but not writable; the crate dir is writable; and Bash is restricted to the whitelisted `cargo +nightly-2025-05-13 ...` form, so even a bare `ls` is refused.

One side effect to note: call 8 left a real file, `probe_inside.txt`, in the crate root. Say the word and I'll remove it — I left it in place since deleting wasn't part of the requested probe set.

No library, interface, test, or C file was modified.
